title: Human hammering with an elastic hammer through a 1-DOF teleoperator with different feedback types
rights: CC0 1.0 in the dataset metadata (Manuel Aiple, TU Delft). The research paper is linked separately; only new derived timing summaries and reader are included.

keys: Human hammering with an elastic hammer through a 1-DOF teleoperator with different feedback types
Increasing Impact by Mechanical Resonance for Teleoperated Hammering

paper.locator: Sections 3.7 and 4.5, Fig. 8, Table 2, and free-air identification. Both versions state 1 kHz; §4.5 and Fig. 8 caption give opposite allocations of the imposed 40 ms to the two directions.

archive.name: data.zip
archive.coverage: Downloaded and validated the full ZIP64 central directory with a 131,072-byte HTTP 206 suffix. Retrieved 14 whole MAT payloads and all fourteen .m scripts via publisher HTTP 206 byte ranges, with archive-member CRC32 checks; full archive MD5 not checked.

selected_author_code.locator: Lines 1–27 and processandplotset.m line 179 compare unit2_posout to the tool-side optical joint angle.

sampling: All six free-air identification files. In the user task, take the lowest numbered right-hand subject in each Latin-square group (1/A, 2/B, 3/C, 4/D), full feedback and delayed full feedback only. File-level scope is four participants; 5-second windows are repeated measurements. ID data and task traces are analyzed separately. Registry metadata describes physical one-DOF devices and an elastic tool. Vicon captures tool joint and tip; none of the six identification files have any rows with both optical markers visible.
method: Use both unit1_velout and unit2_velout on the reported 1 kHz sampling grid. Divide into complete nonoverlapping 5 s windows, drop trailing partial windows. In each compare a fixed 4.8 s central slice of unit 1 against unit 2 at every shift from −100 to +100 samples using Pearson correlation centered separately for each candidate. Require both traces to have standard deviation >=0.1 in their stored velocity scale for all candidate shifts. Record the maximizing lag, correlation, zero-lag correlation. Positive lag means unit 2 follows unit 1. Per-record medians use only eligible windows with maximum correlation >=0.8. Both enabled flags and optical visibility are tabulated as recorded; slave_on is nonzero in only one row per file, so it is not used as a continuous running-state mask.
findings: The 8 task records contain 1,239,746 rows. Baseline full feedback gives median velocity lag 0 ms in each of four participants; the delayed condition gives 32,25,24,26 ms. The 6 identification files have 600,006 rows; with the handle clamped and force feedback disabled one velocity remains constant and no window qualifies. The estimate is relative waveform displacement affected by bilateral mechanics, filters and controller action, not message delivery time. The motion traces lack packet sequence IDs. The full-feedback label, configured 40 ms delay and measured velocity lag are separate quantities.
reproduce: Download data.zip from the fixed source and extract the 14 MAT files named in selected_mats (or use validated ranges). Run python derive_bilateral.py MAT_FOLDER OUT with NumPy and SciPy.

independent_optical_reference.methods: Subset of 8 physical user records. The endstop_translation columns are optical 3D coordinates of the tool joint marker. Compare magnitudes of centered marker displacement speed (mm/s) to the absolute encoder angular displacement rate (rad/s), using the same 2,10,20-ms finite difference span, positive lag when optical marker motion follows device angle. Require entire 5 s windows to be optically visible. Minimum overlapping speed standard deviation 0.1 rad/s and 5 mm/s, Pearson r >=0.8 for reported medians over a ±100 ms search, identical interior comparison length. Report angular steps >π rad/sample; leave the original position values untouched because wrap size and cause are not established. The numerical lag includes optical measurement and processing.
independent_optical_reference.findings: At 10 ms difference span, median lag of the tool-side optical marker relative to device 1 under full feedback was 4,4,4,5 ms across the four groups. Under the nominal 40 ms added delay it was 37,30,29,31 ms. At device 2, the corresponding full-feedback medians were 6,4,4,4 ms and delayed medians unavailable,4,4,4 ms. The first subject’s tool encoder position had 49 one-step changes larger than π in DL (18 in FF); their delayed recording supplies no qualifying same-end marker-to-encoder window at this span. The position discontinuities and empty case are retained. Do not reinterpret the motion lag as a network packet timestamp.
independent_optical_reference.reproduce: python derive_bilateral_optical.py MAT_FOLDER OUT (requires derive_bilateral.py beside it)
